intervals.label: hosting the CHOOZ neutrino experiment (reactor-neutrino site)
intervals.locator: EPJ C 27, 331 (2003) = hep-ex/0301017, section on data taking
intervals.note: Start is the first day of CHOOZ data taking, the earliest dated use of the site; the underground laboratory itself must be older and its construction date was not sourced. Left open because the site went on to host Double Chooz (from 2011 on this record's other interval) and no source says it closed; the idle years 1998-2011 are not documented.
intervals.quote: The data acquisition period extended over 450 days, from 12 March 1997 till 20 July 1998

intervals.label: hosting Double Chooz
intervals.note: No official facility page was reachable (checked 2026-09-17) to source a facility-level founding or operating interval; the start is the same inferred lower bound used for experiment:double-chooz's earliest interval. The site remains a candidate host for other reactor-neutrino work (e.g. NUCLEUS) beyond Double Chooz's own 2017 shutdown, so the interval is left open-ended.
intervals.quote: located at 1050 m from the reactor cores of the Chooz nuclear power plant in France

name: Chooz Reactor Neutrino Site
notes: The Double Chooz official site (double-chooz.fr, doublechooz.in2p3.fr, chooz.in2p3.fr) was unreachable (DNS failure on every domain tried, checked 2026-09-17); this record relies on the 2012 arXiv discovery paper, INSPIRE, and Wikipedia.
experiment:nucleus also uses this facility as its host site.

operator.note: No source consulted (checked 2026-09-17) states an explicit operator distinct from the Double Chooz Collaboration and EDF (which operates the adjacent Chooz Nuclear Power Plant, not the experimental site itself).

summary.plain: The site near the Chooz nuclear power station in northern France where the Double Chooz experiment placed two detectors to catch antineutrinos from the reactors.
summary.technical: Reactor-neutrino site adjacent to the Chooz-B nuclear power plant, Ardennes, France, hosting the Double Chooz near (400 m) and far (1050 m) detector halls.
